The upstream thorlabs_apt package was never installed, imported or run: it loads APT.dll at import time and is Windows-only (README.md:7, thorlabs_apt/core.py:1346-1376), and no hardware was attached. The package is a direct Driver over thorlabs_apt.core:Motor rather than the card's PythonObjectDriver config-only helper: the object exposes status-bit properties, tuple getters and actuator methods, and each writable field needs its own limit. No hardware run and no MHS-Device level is claimed; the evidence is contract_checked on the fake. The fake is an in-memory object with placeholder values, not a recording of a device. Limits: velocity_maximum, acceleration, move_to.position and move_by.distance are Limit.operator_required; the clone reads the velocity and acceleration bounds and the stage travel range from the controller at run time (thorlabs_apt/core.py:395-418, 574-597). site-limits.example.json is an example overlay only, not device data. The hardware limit-switch modes, homing direction and homing limit switch are closed sets cited from the module constants (thorlabs_apt/core.py:9-41). Catalogue classes: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 fixes positions to rad while an APT stage is configured in mm or degrees (STAGE_UNITS_MM = 1, STAGE_UNITS_DEG = 2; thorlabs_apt/core.py:22-26); cap.motion.home.v1 takes axes and speed_scale, which MOT_MoveHome does not accept; cap.motion.stop.v1 declares a deceleration input, which MOT_StopProfiled does not take (thorlabs_apt/core.py:845-852). The extension ids carry these native calls exactly and are listed in catalogue_requests. Safety: the only stop is the native software profiled stop (MOT_StopProfiled); the clone documents no independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set. The package is R1 and the loader does not refuse an unreviewed R1 hardware backend, so an operator must review it before hardware use. Not covered: the hardware path (native.py, APT.dll and the Windows runtime) was never executed; the fake is not a recording. The fake covers the scalar state and the motion/config commands; no array payload is exposed. The stage range, units and velocity bounds are read from the controller and are not asserted here as device facts.
